Most passenger services are recorded as unverified; the model treats them as scenarios (closed, partial, open) rather than as operating.

Ebola Watch does not diagnose, recommend treatments, medicines or vaccines, or assess anyone's symptoms. If someone may be ill or exposed, contact a health professional or your national public-health authority.

Ebola Watch never silently combines these categories, and model estimates are never presented as confirmed cases.

Ebola Watch provides epidemiological observation, burden estimation, forecasting and public-health intelligence. It is not a medical service and does not provide diagnosis, treatment, medicine, vaccine or other clinical advice. Estimates and forecasts are uncertain and must not be used to make decisions about an individual's care.
Established outbreak: substantial confirmed transmission, laboratory-confirmed geographic expansion, or growth.

Estimate the reproduction number of reported cases and project reported cases with uncertainty (renewal model), comparing against a simpler growth model.

Retrospective evaluation (“backtesting”): the model is refitted using only data available at each past date, and its forecasts are compared with what was later reported. Results are shown as computed, including poor ones. Well-calibrated 90% intervals contain the observed value about 90% of the time.
